summary: This document is a formal element-wise TRL readiness and artifact index for the ARGUS-OS1 project, submitted by Jaba Tqemaladze (Georgia Longevity Alliance / UNED Madrid PhD candidate) on 11 November 2026. It describes four workstreams at different TRL levels: a centriole-age inheritance hypothesis (TRL 1), an open imaging instrument (TRL 3–4), an autonomy/data software layer (TRL 4), and a division-rate screening assay concept (TRL 2). The document explicitly states that no biological data has been generated yet, and provides a detailed artifact index, IP status, funding state, and 90-day milestone plan.

content_blocks.title: Document Header and Summary
content_blocks.content:
Title: Element-wise readiness and artifact index, ARGUS-OS1. Submitted by Jaba Tqemaladze, MD — Georgia Longevity Alliance; PhD applicant, UNED Madrid (Programa 9620). Date: 11 Nov 2026.

Summary: Four workstreams at four TRL levels — hypothesis (TRL 1), open imaging instrument (TRL 3–4), autonomy software layer (TRL 4), assay concept (TRL 2). TRL applied per element, not per organisation. Composite reading: biology TRL 1, platform TRL 4. Biological workstream has produced no data. No target, no molecule, no intervention. IP: three method claims identified but unfiled by choice. Open licences (Apache-2.0, CERN-OHL-S, CC-BY) cover hardware, firmware fork, and documentation.

content_blocks.title: Section 1 — Scope of the Claim
content_blocks.content: Explicit scope statement: no assays, no imaging runs, no biological datasets in the biological workstream. The instrument has not yet produced a division-timing dataset. The step from centriole age to a therapeutic mechanism is a hypothesis with a written falsification condition. All numbers in the document are to be read within these boundaries.

content_blocks.title: Section 2 — Four Workstreams, Four Readiness Levels
content_blocks.content:
TRL defined per technology element/subsystem (NASA NPR 7123.1; Horizon Europe TRL annex).

| Workstream | TRL | What exists | What moves it |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 — Centriole-age inheritance hypothesis | 1 | Hypothesis, falsification condition, statistical plan, pre-registrable protocol | First 20 tracked divisions in immortalized fibroblasts |
| W2 — Open imaging instrument | 3–4 | OpenFlexure fork (community base at TRL 9); BOM closed; subsystems validated one by one; hardware focus hold over multi-day runs unvalidated, flagged as P0 | Fiducial autofocus prototype, 72 h drift test |
| W3 — Autonomy and data software | 4 | TRD v0.9b frozen; grammar core with 29 passing unit tests (12 pytest, 17 Rust) — corrected 12 Nov 2026 from earlier unsupported figure of 91; motor-release patch tested 5/5 against a live microscope server and sent upstream | Unattended end-to-end run producing a tracked-division log |
| W4 — Division-rate screening endpoint | 2 | Assay logic, statistics, readout method specified | Reproducibility across two cell lines |

Key note: Platform (W2, W3) is not an idea; biology (W1) is not evidence. One composite number erases the difference.

content_blocks.title: Section 3 — Artifact Index (What Can Be Opened Today)
content_blocks.content:
Two of four workstreams ship inspectable artifacts. Full list:
- docs/ARGUS_TRD_v0.9b.md — technical requirements document, frozen
- hardware/ARGUS-OS1_BOM.csv — bill of materials, closed
- hardware/ARGUS-OS1_TESTING.md, hardware/CLEANING_OPTICS.md — test and handling procedures
- software/microscope/motor_release_sangaboard.patch — 5/5 tests passing, endpoint confirmed in Thing Description, submitted upstream 12 Aug 2026; accompanied by written correspondence with OpenFlexure maintainers
- software/argus_mhs, software/argus-agent, software/tests — autonomy layer, unit-tested
- docs/ARGUS_Protocol_Hayflick_Limit_Immortalized_Fibroblasts.md — planned experiment, written for pre-registration
- docs/ARGUS_label_free_centriole_assignment.md — readout method
- docs/AXIO_OBSERVER_ENGINEERING_ANALYSIS_2026-10-19.md — benchmark against Zeiss Axio Observer 7 plus Nikon PFS, Olympus TruFocus, Leica AFC, IncuCyte, with capability gaps and open fixes
- docs/ARGUS_Literature_Analysis_EN.md, EVIDENCE.md, THEORY.md, PARAMETERS.md — literature base with verified identifiers, evidence table, theory, parameters

None of it is biological validation. All artifacts are publicly inspectable in the repository.

content_blocks.title: Section 4 — Intellectual Property: Three Corrections, One Gate
content_blocks.content:
Open licences (Apache-2.0, CERN-OHL-S, CC-BY) cover hardware design, firmware fork, and documentation. They do NOT cover method claims.

Three unfiled method claim candidates (unfiled by choice):
(a) Centriole-age-resolved division timing as a screening readout
(b) Label-free centriole assignment pipeline
(c) Fiducial-based focus hold for multi-day live imaging on an open stage

Rationale for not filing: filing before the pilot would be a spend with no evidence behind it.

Decision gate: If the pilot reaches the primary endpoint fixed in the protocol before data collection, a provisional application on candidate (a) is filed within 60 days of that result. Filing cost is already line-itemed in the budget.

IP-NFT: described as a governance and data-rights instrument giving holders claims on data and downstream licensing decisions. Investor value is untested; not offered as a patent substitute.

Partner licensing value: what a pharma partner licenses is a validated protocol, a reference dataset, and reproducible instrumentation — not a patent on the instrument. Open licences lower partner's cost of reproducing the assay, raising the value of the reference dataset.

content_blocks.title: Section 5 — Team, Funding and Backing
content_blocks.content:
State of record: small team, single-programmer dependency on the software layer, no institutional backing beyond a small Georgian nonprofit (Georgia Longevity Alliance), no active funding at time of writing.

Software evidence: 29 unit tests (12 pytest, 17 Rust), two rerunnable commands, frozen TRD v0.9b (14 Oct 2026), one upstream patch with maintainer correspondence. Count and commands in TRL evidence pack of 12 November 2026.

Grant applications submitted and pending:
- Open Source Collective: USD 17,000, submitted 1 Aug 2026
- Foresight: USD 50,050, submitted 31 Jul 2026

Grant outcomes:
- Open Source Collective (USD 17,000) — pending
- Foresight (USD 50,050) — pending
- Sovereign Tech Fund — declined 10 Nov 2026 on prevalence criterion (funds components other projects already depend on); resubmission not planned before Q4 2027

Partnerships: Correspondence with a centriole-biology group in the United States about tracking and TIAM1. No signed agreement; not presented as institutional backing.

content_blocks.title: Section 6 — Therapeutic Pathway, Step by Step
content_blocks.content:
| Step | Claim | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Centriole age at birth predicts the interdivision interval | Hypothesis, falsifiable, untested |
| 2 | Asymmetric inheritance biases which daughter keeps the renewal-competent state | Literature-grounded, untested in this system |
| 3 | Division-timing drift is a measurable senescence-adjacent phenotype | Assay designed, no data |
| 4 | That phenotype screens senolytics, senomorphics, autophagy activators | Concept, TRL 2 |
| 5 | A validated endpoint becomes a licensed assay for aging-focused discovery | Downstream of this phase; not offered here |

Steps 1–4 are the project. Step 5 is downstream and not part of this phase — listed only to make the boundary of the claim visible, not as proximity credit for therapy.

content_blocks.title: Section 7 — Ninety Days, Dated and Checkable
content_blocks.content:
Planned milestones with hard dates:
1. Fiducial autofocus prototype on the OpenFlexure fork; 72 h focus-hold test with drift logged — 15 Jan 2027
2. Protocol pre-registration deposited publicly before the first imaging run — before data collection (no fixed date, conditional)
3. Unattended end-to-end run producing a machine-readable tracked-division log on fixed samples — 31 Jan 2027
4. Second contributor on the software layer, advisory or paid — 28 Feb 2027
5. Re-assessment request with items 1–3 attached — 1 Mar 2027

Conditional clause: If items 1–3 slip past those dates, the corresponding workstream stays where it is, the artifact is published with its measured values, and the next purchase is not made.

key_findings: Four workstreams at distinct TRL levels: W1 (centriole-age hypothesis) = TRL 1, W2 (open imaging instrument) = TRL 3–4, W3 (autonomy/data software) = TRL 4, W4 (division-rate screening endpoint) = TRL 2.
No biological data has been generated; the instrument has not yet produced a division-timing dataset. The biological workstream is purely at the hypothesis stage.
W3 software layer has 29 passing unit tests (12 pytest, 17 Rust); motor-release patch tested 5/5 against a live microscope server and submitted upstream to OpenFlexure on 12 Aug 2026.

W2 imaging instrument is based on an OpenFlexure fork (community base TRL 9); BOM closed; subsystems validated individually; hardware focus hold over multi-day runs is unvalidated and flagged as P0 priority issue.

Three method claims identified but deliberately unfiled: (a) centriole-age-resolved division timing as screening readout, (b) label-free centriole assignment pipeline, (c) fiducial-based focus hold for multi-day live imaging. Filing gated on pilot reaching primary endpoint.
Provisional patent application on candidate (a) to be filed within 60 days of pilot reaching primary endpoint; filing cost already budgeted.
No active funding; two grants pending: Open Source Collective (USD 17,000, submitted 1 Aug 2026) and Foresight (USD 50,050, submitted 31 Jul 2026). Sovereign Tech Fund declined 10 Nov 2026.
Single-programmer dependency on software layer; no institutional backing beyond Georgia Longevity Alliance nonprofit.
Therapeutic pathway is 5 steps; steps 1–4 are the project scope; step 5 (licensed assay) is explicitly downstream and not claimed in this phase.
TRD v0.9b frozen 14 Oct 2026; earlier unit test count of 91 was corrected to 29 on 12 Nov 2026.
Benchmark analysis conducted against Zeiss Axio Observer 7, Nikon PFS, Olympus TruFocus, Leica AFC, and IncuCyte, with capability gaps and open fixes documented.
Correspondence with a US centriole-biology group about tracking and TIAM1; no signed agreement.
